answer: Payout-sink merging: each agent binds one withdrawal address, and the indexer traces rewards 3 hops out over a 14-day window. Agents whose earnings converge on a common sink are merged into one juniper-style cluster paid a single share, split evenly. So N fakes earn about 1/N each unless the operator keeps N separate cash-out paths, each needing its own exchange account, a pearl that costs real money and KYC, so cost grows linearly while payout stays flat. Weakness: a gale of mixers or OTC hops can launder past 3 hops, and honest agents paid into one custodial hot wallet get wrongly merged.
